subject: Billing behavior for interleaved long-context streams + heartbeat

From: Michaela Torres <michaela@bluepeakhealth.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing question: interleaved streaming sessions, heartbeat & rounding

Hi Avery,

We're doing a short pilot of the Redwood streaming API for our patient-chat transcripts. A couple of implementation details came up and I wanted to confirm how billing units are applied so we can forecast costs: 

1) We keep a long context (up to ~40k tokens) on the server, but client interactions are often short bursts: e.g., user sends a 20-token query, we stream 100 tokens back, then 30 minutes later another 15-token prompt.

2) We considered sending a small heartbeat every 5 minutes to keep the KV cache warm for the session. Does a heartbeat that contains no user-visible tokens still consume billing units?

3) How do you round minimums for microbursts? If we have a per-call minimum of N tokens, is that applied to each streamed response chunk or the full logical interaction across the session? Example: three separate short responses in a 24-hour window — do those get billed separately or aggregated?

If useful, we can share a sample of our event timing distribution. We're trying to decide whether to implement prefix caching locally or rely on your KV cache.

Thanks,
Michaela
Director of Platform Engineering
BluePeak Health

Hi Michaela — thanks for the clear examples, they help a lot. Quick answers up front, then Marissa can give the official billing policy and calculations: 

- Heartbeat tokens: small heartbeats (e.g., a keepalive call with zero prompt/token output) are treated as API calls and will count toward metering if they touch the model runtime. We often recommend an API-side TTL for KV entries rather than frequent heartbeats.

- Aggregation vs per-call minimums: We support session aggregation for flows that are explicitly bound to the same session id and fall within a configurable aggregation window. By default that window is 12 hours for Hosted plans and 24 hours for Dedicated/Private — within that window streamed responses and prompts tied to the same session id are rolled up for billing before minimums are applied. Outside of the window they are billed separately.

- Rounding: Billing is tokenized and rounded up to the billing quantum (default 1 token), and we apply a per-call floor only after aggregation. Example below.

Marissa — can you confirm the current default aggregation windows and sample math for the BP pilot? Ben — once we have the official numbers, we can propose a pilot concession if needed.

Avery Johnson
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Michaela,

Thanks — below is the formal policy and a worked example attached (billing_calculation_matrix.xlsx). TL;DR: if you use a session id and operations fall within the pilot aggregation window, they aggregate before minimums. Heartbeats that do not create tokens but hit the model runtime are billable at a small fixed cost.

Policy details (current defaults for Hosted pilot customers):
- Aggregation window: 12 hours (events with same session id aggregated). Dedicated/Private defaults: 24 hours (can be configured).
- Billing quantum: 1 token. No fractional tokens are billed.
- Per-aggregation minimum (floor): 50 tokens. Applied after aggregation. I.e., if your aggregated session usage is 38 tokens, you are billed 50.
- Heartbeat behavior: A heartbeat call that does not send a prompt but pings the runtime still incurs a minimal metered unit equal to 5 tokens (this covers runtime startup/keepalive GPU cycles). If you instead use a purely client-side TTL and avoid hitting the runtime, there is no charge.

Worked example (attached matrix shows variations):
Scenario A (three microbursts within 12h window, same session id):
  - Prompt 1: 20 tokens in, 100 tokens out => 120 tokens
  - Prompt 2: 15 tokens in, 40 tokens out => 55 tokens
  - Prompt 3: 10 tokens in, 30 tokens out => 40 tokens
  - Aggregated total = 215 tokens => billed 215 tokens (no floor applied because >50).

Scenario B (two tiny bursts, 18 hours apart):
  - Burst 1: 6 tokens in, 20 tokens out => 26 tokens -> billed 50 (floor) if not aggregated
  - Burst 2: 5 tokens in, 10 tokens out => 15 tokens -> billed 50 (floor)
  - If session id were preserved and window extended to 24h (Dedicated), total 41 tokens -> billed 50 once.

Heartbeat example:
  - If you send a heartbeat every 5 minutes for 12h (144 heartbeats) that touch the runtime: 144 * 5 token-units = 720 token-equivalents (billed).
  - If you instead use a passive TTL and only hit the runtime on real prompts, cost is just the real prompts.

Attachments: billing_calculation_matrix.xlsx (sample math), sample_invoice_example.pdf (illustrative invoice).

If you'd like, Ben and I can prepare a short cost model using your real event distribution.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal Billing Manager, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: billing_calculation_matrix.xlsx)

Hi Michaela — following up with a suggested pilot concession to keep your costs predictable during the proof-of-concept.

Proposal outline:
- Pilot term: 60 days.
- Billing floor override: For the pilot we will apply a per-session monthly minimum of 10,000 token credits (applied to aggregated usage per session id) instead of per-call floors for any session flagged as "BP-POC". This replaces the 50-token floor for aggregated sessions and prevents microbursts from driving unexpected per-call floors.
- Heartbeat guidance: Recommend switching to client-side TTL with a 24h server-side retention where possible. If heartbeats are unavoidable, we can map heartbeat counts to a capped credit (e.g., cap of 5,000 token-equivalents per session per month for the pilot).
